The Dubliners perform folk ballad "Dublin In the Rare Old Times" in the pub

The 1960's saw a revival of folk music in Ireland. This end of the revival was mainly urban (Dublin especially), unlike traditional music which was mainly rural, and fronted by socialist working class Dubs. This is the music of the Irish tradition that I would relate to most, being a working class Dubliner myself. This is the music in the pubs I patronise and the lyrics and sentiments speak much more to my experiences. This part of the folk revival tried to rid the music of elitism, due to traditional musics very high difficulty among a lot of other things. This song is my favourite of the ballads also as growing up I saw the last of the big changes in Dublin before the Celtic Tiger pounced and dragged us into materialism and greed. We lost a lot of character and Irishness and it happened before my eyes.

The Dubliners exemplify the ballad scene more than any. Unfortunately the singer, Ronnie Drew, has since died, but he's still considered one of Dublin's greatest.
